frequency_question: How often does the Federal Reserve Board of Governors successfully raise macroprudential buffers above their structural zero baseline over a multi-year horizon?
membership_rule: Includes formal rulemakings or adjustments to the Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB) or equivalent systemic capital add-ons by the Fed; excludes standard microprudential capital requirement updates (like regular stress test iterations or Basel III endgame routine modifications unless they actively shift the CCyB rate).

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named formal review instances covering the entire history of the operational CCyB framework in the United States.
known_gaps: The framework has never been activated above 0%, providing zero historical instances of successful upward transition from the dormant baseline.
skeleton: Total formal review cycles of the CCyB rate since its institutionalization vs. cycles resulting in a non-zero hike
validity_reason: The structural inertia and institutional reluctance to activate the CCyB remain consistent across regulatory leadership turns until a major overhaul of the macroprudential framework occurs.
